To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of location based services can lead to the identification of users, even if their identity is not explicitly revealed to the service provider and that it is possible to design location-based systems that protect user privacy against this threat.

(1) the use of location services may reveal sensitive information about users; (2) the risk depends on several factors, such as the number of users in the database and the number of location requests made by each user; (3) the use of a random perturbation technique, based on the concept of k-anonymity, can effectively prevent the risk of revealing sensitive information about users.
